name: Mewing
summary: Resting the whole tongue against the palate to reshape the face; popular online, but no research shows it changes adult jaw structure.
lead: Mewing is a self-directed practice in which a person rests the whole tongue against the roof of the mouth, keeps the lips sealed and the teeth lightly together, and breathes through the nose, with the stated aim of improving jaw and facial structure . It takes its name from John Mew, a British orthodontist, and his son Mike Mew, who promoted the approach known as orthotropics .
claims: Mewing can bring the maxilla forward and sharpen the jawline
Mewing mostly works in childhood and does little after puberty
Mewing temporarily lifts the hyoid and tightens the jawline's look
Mewing can harm the face

name: Hard mewing
summary: Mewing with deliberate upward tongue pressure; discussed as a stronger version of tongue posture, with no research testing it and some users reporting masseter growth.
lead: Hard mewing is a term used in looksmaxxing communities for a more forceful form of mewing, in which a person presses the tongue upward against the palate with deliberate effort rather than simply resting it there . Forum users use it interchangeably with, or as a stage beyond, ordinary mewing, and some threads ask directly how the two differ .
claims: Hard mewing causes forward growth even after puberty
Hard mewing widens the jaw or enlarges the masseters
Hard mewing combined with thumb pulling and expanders produces visible change

name: Thumb pulling
summary: Pulling the palate downward with a thumb to widen the upper jaw; discussed as a free substitute for expanders, with no studies behind it.
lead: Thumb pulling is a practice in looksmaxxing communities in which a person pulls on the palate with the thumb, usually downward and forward, in the belief that it can widen the palate or move the maxilla forward . It is discussed as a free alternative to professional palatal expansion and is commonly paired with mewing and chewing.
claims: Thumb pulling can widen the palate or advance the maxilla
It only works before about 15 or 16
A thumb cannot generate enough force to matter
Thumb pulling can create a diastema or other tooth changes

name: Chewing for jaw
summary: Chewing tough gum or food to build the masseters and jaw; muscle enlargement is documented, bone change is untested.
lead: Chewing for jaw, also called jawmaxxing, is a practice in looksmaxxing communities in which people chew hard gum, particularly mastic gum, or tough foods to develop the jaw muscles and, according to proponents, the jaw's appearance . It is often paired with mewing, chin tucks and neck exercises .
claims: Chewing hard gum builds the masseters and defines the jaw
Chewing and tongue posture together reshape the jaw bone and bring the maxilla forward
Heavy chewing can backfire

name: Facial yoga / face exercises
summary: Muscle exercises for the face promoted as a natural facelift; the available sources include no study of appearance outcomes.
lead: Facial yoga, also called face exercises, is a set of voluntary facial-muscle movements promoted to firm, lift or reshape the face, and is often presented as a natural alternative to cosmetic procedures. In looksmaxxing forums it is discussed for the cheekbones, nose, chin and jawline .
claims: Chin and jaw exercises can produce visible change
Face exercises are a lesser substitute for surgery or appliances
Fat loss and chewing do more than face exercises

name: Wolff's law facial loading
summary: The idea that mechanical load remodels facial bone, borrowed from a real principle of bone biology but untested for tongue posture, chewing or pulling.
lead: Wolff's law states that bone in a healthy animal adapts to the loads placed on it, becoming denser and stronger under greater loading and weaker under less . It is named for the German surgeon and anatomist Julius Wolff (1836-1902), whose 1892 book Das Gesetz der Transformation der Knochen set out the idea . In looksmaxxing communities, 'Wolff's law' is cited as the reason that mewing, chewing, thumb pulling and similar practices are said to reshape the face.
claims: Facial bones remodel under mechanical load, so loading the face can reshape it
Facial sutures never fuse, so adults can still grow the face
Greater force means more bone change

name: Orbital rubbing / eye socket massage
summary: Pressing or rubbing the eye socket to reshape the eyes; no studies support bone change, and eye rubbing is linked to corneal problems.
lead: Orbital rubbing, also called eye socket massage, is a bonehacking practice in which a person presses or rubs the area around the eye socket in the belief that doing so can change the shape or position of the orbit and therefore the appearance of the eyes. It is discussed as a non-surgical way to alter eye-area aesthetics.

name: Nose bone massaging / nasal bone pushing
summary: Pressing or massaging the nose to narrow it; no study supports reshaping and medical literature covers only fractures.
lead: Nose bone massaging, or nasal bone pushing, is a bonehacking practice in which a person presses or massages the nose, usually the bridge, in the belief that this can narrow it or change its shape without surgery.

name: Hyoid / neck posture meta
summary: Raising the hyoid or fixing neck posture for a sharper jawline; no studies address appearance, only airway anatomy.
lead: The hyoid or neck posture meta is a set of beliefs in looksmaxxing communities that the position of the hyoid bone, together with neck posture and submental fat, determines the sharpness of the jawline and neck in profile. Users describe a "low" or "bad" hyoid as flattening the angle between chin and neck, and they discuss ways to "raise" it.
claims: A low or prominent hyoid ruins the side profile
Chin tucks and neck exercises can raise the hyoid
Tongue posture and mewing change the hyoid and jaw area

name: Palate expanders (adult)
summary: Adult MARPE or surgical palate expansion for midface width and breathing; real orthodontic procedure, but appearance benefit is untested.
lead: Palate expanders are orthodontic devices that widen the upper jaw (maxilla) so that upper and lower teeth fit together better. They are most often used in children and adolescents, and adult versions, such as miniscrew-assisted rapid palatal expansion (MARPE) and surgically assisted expansion, are used for transverse maxillary deficiency in patients whose palatal suture has matured .
claims: Expanding the palate widens the face and improves aesthetics
Adults can achieve skeletal expansion without surgery
Expansion improves breathing
Tongue posture alone can widen the palate

name: Nasal breathing meta
summary: Breathing through the nose for better facial development; child studies link mouth breathing to growth changes, adult appearance effects are untested.
lead: The nasal breathing meta is the looksmaxxing belief that habitually breathing through the nose, rather than the mouth, supports healthy facial development, jaw and midface structure, and appearance. It is closely associated with mewing, mouth taping and discussions of nasal surgery.
claims: Mouth breathing narrows the face and recedes the jaw
Switching to nasal breathing as an adult improves facial appearance
Mouth taping helps maintain nasal breathing during sleep
Surgery or expansion can fix nasal breathing problems

name: Sleeping position for face symmetry
summary: Sleeping on your back to keep the face symmetrical; no study links sleep posture to facial symmetry.
lead: Sleeping position for face symmetry is a looksmaxxing belief that the posture a person sleeps in affects facial symmetry, with sleeping on the back often described as the way to avoid asymmetry caused by pressing one side of the face into a pillow.

name: Cortisol face / stress face claims
summary: The idea that stress hormones puff up and age your face; the medical 'moon face' is real but tied to sustained hormone excess, and nothing tests everyday stress.
lead: 'Cortisol face' or 'stress face' is an informal term for a rounded, puffy or aged-looking face that some people attribute to stress and elevated levels of the hormone cortisol. Cortisol is the main glucocorticoid released in response to stress and low blood sugar; it raises blood glucose, mobilises energy stores, suppresses inflammation and increases sodium and water retention.
claims: Chronic stress and high cortisol make the face puffy and aged ('cortisol face').
Social and school stress produce 'cortisol spikes' that make you feel and look worse.
Medical-grade facial rounding is a real effect of too much cortisol.

name: Limb lengthening surgery (LL)
summary: Cutting and gradually extending the femurs or tibias to add height; the only route to permanent added stature, but it is major surgery with months of recovery and documented complications.
lead: Limb lengthening, often abbreviated 'LL' in looksmaxxing communities, is a surgical method that increases the length of a limb bone by cutting it and slowly separating the two ends while new bone and soft tissue form between them. This biological process is called distraction osteogenesis. It is used in medicine for limb-length discrepancy, deformity correction, bone defects and skeletal dysplasias such as achondroplasia, and is also performed electively for cosmetic height gain.
claims: LL is the only way to gain real, permanent height after growth plates close.
India is the cheapest 'legit' place to have LL done.
Internal nails give a smoother recovery than external frames.
LL is a major life-changing upgrade for dating and status.

name: Cosmetic leg lengthening (Precice nails)
summary: Height surgery using a magnetically lengthened nail inside the bone instead of an external frame; well studied for medical lengthening, with limited cosmetic-specific data.
lead: The Precice nail is a motorless, magnetically driven intramedullary (inside-the-bone) lengthening nail made by Ellipse Technologies, later NuVasive. An external remote control uses a magnet to lengthen the implant in small controlled increments after the bone has been cut, so the bone grows longer through distraction osteogenesis without an external fixator. A 2014 study of the device noted that earlier internal lengthening designs had imprecise distraction, with nerve injuries, joint contractures and nonunion, and that the magnet-operated Precice nail had recently been cleared by the FDA.

name: HGH for height
summary: Using growth hormone to try to grow taller; studied in children with short stature, with modest gains, and untested for healthy adults with closed growth plates.
lead: Human growth hormone (HGH), also called somatropin, is a peptide hormone produced by the pituitary gland and available as a recombinant prescription drug. 'HGH for height' refers to using it to increase stature, either in children who are short without a hormone deficiency (so-called idiopathic short stature) or, in looksmaxxing communities, by people who hope to gain height beyond what they would reach naturally.
claims: HGH can still add height even if you are past puberty.
Growth-hormone-releasing peptides (CJC-1295, ipamorelin) or IGF-1 LR3 can substitute for HGH for height.
HGH causes facial changes such as a wider nose.
There is a right way to cycle HGH (on/off schedules, subcutaneous versus intramuscular).

name: Letrozole / aromatase inhibitors for height
summary: Using aromatase inhibitors to slow bone maturation and extend growth; trialled in boys with short stature, with no published evidence for healthy adults.
lead: Aromatase inhibitors (AIs) are drugs that block aromatase, the enzyme that converts androgens such as testosterone into oestrogens. Letrozole and anastrozole are reversible nonsteroidal inhibitors, and exemestane is an irreversible steroidal one. They are approved mainly for hormone-receptor-positive breast cancer in postmenopausal women.

name: Hanging / stretching for height
summary: Hanging and stretching to decompress the spine for height; any gain reported is brief, and no trial tests lasting growth in adults.
lead: Hanging or stretching for height is a practice in height-focused looksmaxxing communities in which people hang from a bar, use traction or stretching routines, or otherwise aim to decompress the spine in the hope of gaining or recovering height. It is also discussed under the terms decompression and spinal decompression. The underlying idea is that gravity compresses the intervertebral discs over the day and that sustained traction can restore or add length to the spine.

name: Height-increasing supplements
summary: OTC pills sold to make you taller; height is mostly genetic and no trial backs them for adults.
lead: Height-increasing supplements are over-the-counter products, typically vitamin, mineral, amino-acid or herbal blends, marketed with the claim that they help people grow taller or reach their genetic height potential. They are discussed in height-focused looksmaxxing communities, where users ask whether growth pills work for teenagers or adults.
claims: Growth supplements can help people grow taller or reach full potential.
Supplements are too expensive and slow to be worth it.

name: Squatmaxxing / spinal loading
summary: Squat-focused leg training; discussed for physique proportions, with no source tying it to height.
lead: Squatmaxxing is looksmaxxing slang for building the legs and lower body through squats, either to improve physique proportions or, in some discussions, to affect how tall or strong a person looks. A looksmax.org thread titled Squatmaxxing asks whether leg development suits people with a wide waist, and a reply asks the original poster about body fat percentage, gym training and height.
claims: Squatting and leg development help people who are wide-waisted.

name: Raw milk for height
summary: Drinking unpasteurised milk to grow taller; no height studies exist and the CDC and FDA advise against it.
lead: Raw milk for height refers to the belief, circulating in some height-focused online circles under slogans such as Raw Milk + Healthy = Holy Height, that drinking unpasteurised milk promotes growth. Wikipedia defines raw milk as milk that has not been pasteurised and reports that proponents say it tastes better, is more nutritious and supports immunity.

name: Height-stretching devices / inversion
summary: Inversion tables and stretch devices for height; any gain reported is millimetres and short-lived.
lead: Height-stretching devices are products marketed or discussed as ways to add height by stretching or decompressing the spine. The best-known examples are inversion tables and gravity boots, which suspend a person at an inverted angle as a form of gravity-assisted spinal traction. In looksmaxxing communities, inversion tables are discussed as a possible way to gain or hold morning height.
claims: An inversion table can add about two inches of morning height.
Glucosamine could help keep the height gained from inversion.
Inversion only decompresses the spine and is a cope.

name: Posture for height (rib/pelvic tilt)
summary: Correcting pelvic tilt and rib flare to recover height; forum anecdotes, but no study measures stature change.
lead: Posture for height is the belief in looksmaxxing communities that correcting pelvic tilt, rib flare or related posture patterns can add centimetres to standing height. Forum threads on anterior pelvic tilt (APT) ask whether fixing it would increase height, how to correct it, and whether tilt asymmetry affects facial symmetry.
claims: Fixing anterior pelvic tilt can add inches of height.
Pelvic tilt can be fixed with stretching in weeks.
Pelvic or shoulder tilt causes facial asymmetry.

name: Growth-plate peptides (IGF-1/MK-677 for height)
summary: Growth hormone secretagogues like MK-677 (and IGF-1 products) pitched as a way to gain height; trials exist only in children with growth hormone deficiency, none in healthy short people.
lead: Growth-plate peptides is a looksmaxxing term for the use of growth hormone (GH) secretagogues and related products, chiefly MK-677 (ibutamoren) and IGF-1, with the aim of increasing height. MK-677 is an experimental, orally active drug that stimulates the ghrelin receptor and raises GH and IGF-1 levels.

name: Manlet / height tiers
summary: Community slang for short men and the height brackets used to rank them; mostly a social-hierarchy vocabulary with height a major topic in appearance discourse.
lead: Manlet is slang used on looksmaxxing forums such as looksmax.org for a man considered short, often used with the idea of height tiers: informal brackets of height used to rank men within the community. Posters disagree about where the thresholds sit, and threads exist both asserting and disputing particular cutoffs.
claims: Being short is a major, hard-to-change disadvantage (the 'heightpill').
Drugs like MK-677 can add height for a teenager who is short.
Confidence and presentation can offset height.

name: Anabolic steroid stacks (looksmaxxing)
summary: Combinations of anabolic-androgenic steroids and other hormones that forum users discuss for a more muscular, masculine look; documented in medicine mainly for harms and hormonal suppression.
lead: Anabolic steroid stacks are combinations of anabolic-androgenic steroids (AAS), often taken with other hormones, that users on looksmaxxing forums discuss for building muscle and a masculine appearance. Anabolic-androgenic steroids are drugs structurally related to testosterone that act by binding to and activating the androgen receptor.
claims: A well-designed stack can improve facial masculinity and skeletal width during or after puberty.
Stacks can be chosen to avoid infertility and hormone shutdown.
Adding growth hormone, thyroid hormone, insulin or SARMs to a stack improves the result.

name: Short steroid cycles myth
summary: The belief that brief steroid courses avoid the lasting harms of long ones; no trial has tested it for appearance use, and medical sources describe recovery as variable.
lead: The short steroid cycles claim holds that brief courses of anabolic-androgenic steroids are comparatively safe. It is a belief about how duration relates to risk rather than a defined practice.

name: TRT / testosterone for jaw
summary: The idea of using testosterone or related androgens to masculinise the jaw and face; testosterone therapy is established for low testosterone, but no study tests it for jaw structure.
lead: TRT or testosterone for jaw refers to the belief, discussed in looksmaxxing communities, that testosterone replacement or related androgens such as DHT can masculinise the jaw and other facial structure. Testosterone medication is used to treat males with low or absent natural production, for masculinising hormone therapy and for certain breast cancers.

name: DHT / Androgel for facial structure
summary: Topical DHT or testosterone gel pitched in forums for masculinising the face during puberty; gels are studied for low testosterone in older men, not for facial structure.
lead: DHT gel and AndroGel for facial structure is a hormonal protocol discussed on looksmaxxing forums. Dihydrotestosterone (DHT) is an androgen made from testosterone by 5-alpha-reductase in target tissues, and it acts mainly locally. It is associated with facial and body hair, prostate and genital development. AndroGel is a testosterone gel approved for male hypogonadism.
claims: Topical DHT during puberty enhances masculine facial bone development.
DHT gel is among the safest looksmaxxing tools.

name: Pentastack
summary: A five-drug stimulant and depressant mix from 2026 livestream culture; a news event more than a looks method.
lead: The pentastack is a term for a five-substance drug combination that came to wider attention in 2026 through looksmaxxing influencers. According to Wikipedia, it consists of Adderall (amphetamine salts), dextromethorphan, pregabalin, ketamine and 1,4-butanediol (BDO), and it combines a stimulant with several central nervous system depressants.
claims: The pentastack is a 'healthy, sustainable' drug stack.
It helps users feel 'neurotypical' in public.
